messages:
Alex Kim: Heads-up — saw a regressed p95 on Dedicated when running the long-tail synth. Old batching p95 ~120ms, new batching heuristic p95 ~330ms. Repro on r-staging-3.
Priya Desai: ugh, which run id/config?
Alex Kim: run id 2026-03-18-11:12, config attached below. main diff: dynamic_merge_threshold enabled.
Alex Kim: ```json
{
  "loadgen": {
    "qps_ramp": {
      "start": 50,
      "peak": 1600,
      "pattern": "staircase",
      "step_ms": 20000
    },
    "burst": {
      "type": "pareto_spikes",
      "alpha": 1.3,
      "spike_qps": 6000
    },
    "tail_shape": "pareto",
    "kv_prewarm": false,
    "seed": 42
  },
  "server_flags": {
    "dynamic_merge_threshold": true,
    "max_merge_delay_ms": 5
  }
}
```
Miguel Torres: bench-bot uploaded a quick comparison (staging) -> https://bench.internal/compare/3749999999 (perf csv + flame). kernel-switch churn looks high in the trace.
bench-bot: automated run summary: baseline p95=118ms, new-heuristic p95=328ms, 12% throughput drop at peak, KV hit-rate dropped from 84% -> 61% during spikes.
Sara Nguyen: that KV hit-rate drop is suspicious — if the cache wasn't warmed it will force lots of large KV fetches and bigger batches + kernel fallbacks. Did we prewarm prefix cache?
Alex Kim: no prewarm in this run, intended to emulate cold-start long-tail. But regression still unexpected vs prior cold-start runs.
Jamal Reed: I looked at the kernel logs. On many requests we flip from quant-fast -> matmul-fallback mid-stream because seq_len estimate changes after KV materialized. memcpy dominates. flame graph: /artifacts/flame-3749999999.svg shows memcpy ~28% of op time.
Linh Zhao: sequence estimation changing during request is a vector — once KV returns we extend sequence and kernel selection recomputes, causing expensive re-dispatch. We should: 1) stabilize kernel choice until KV resolves or 2) pre-reserve a low-latency kernel for uncertain seq length.
Priya Desai: for apples-to-apples we need identical kernel-selection config + identical KV state. Add kernel_randomize=false and run with kv_prewarm=true/false pairs.
Miguel Torres: agreed. Proposed experiment matrix:
- A: old-batcher + kv_prewarm=true
- B: new-heuristic + kv_prewarm=true
- C: old-batcher + kv_prewarm=false
- D: new-heuristic + kv_prewarm=false
Keep same seed and ramp profile.
Linh Zhao: also add a variant E where we set max_merge_delay_ms=3 and prefer_low_latency_kernel=true to see impact on tail. small tweak, easy rollback.
Alex Kim: command I'll run in staging (feel free to reuse):
```bash
./loadgen --config loadgen-config.json --replay --seed 42 --prewarm 120 --output /tmp/bench-3749999999
# server flags: --dynamic_merge_threshold=on --kernel_randomize=false
```
Sara Nguyen: can we instrument a KV-wait histogram in the runtime? want to see correlation between KV latency and kernel reselect.
Jamal Reed: added a quick probe in tracing: kv.wait_ms bucketed per-request. initial traces show heavy tail at 200-800ms during pareto spikes.
bench-bot: queued matrix runs A..E, estimated run time 45m each, will post CSV and flamegraphs to /bench/3749999999 when done.
Priya Desai: note for results: ensure same model variant and quantization path — kernel selection differs if we fall back to non-quant path. add flag --force-kernel-path=quant where applicable.
Miguel Torres: pointer: use this loadgen tweak to reproduce long-tail shaping locally: --arrival-dist pareto --pareto-alpha 1.3 --spike-interval 30s --staircase-steps 8
Linh Zhao: short mitigation idea: hold initial kernel decision for t_hold_ms=10ms (give KV a chance) then if no KV response, proceed. That avoids mid-request re-dispatchs in most cases. cheap to implement.
Alex Kim: can we try t_hold_ms=10 in one of the runs?
Linh Zhao: yes, will add as variant F (new-heuristic + t_hold=10ms + kv_prewarm=false).
ops-bot: scheduled: staging-run-3749999999 at 11:30 UTC by Miguel Torres.
Priya Desai: recording action items: (1) Miguel run matrix A..F and upload CSV/flame (owner Miguel), (2) Linh prototype t_hold patch and bench locally (owner Linh), (3) Jamal add KV-wait histogram to tracing (owner Jamal), (4) Alex coordinate apples-to-apples (owner Alex).
Alex Kim: thanks everyone — let's reconvene after bench outputs. quick note: if we see memcpy still hot, suspect batching merge logic producing large contiguous memcpy targets; we may need to cap merge size or prefer fragmented IO for long reqs.
Sara Nguyen: ack. I'll keep an eye on ops alerts.
Miguel Torres: starting run now, will post link when CSVs are ready.
bench-bot: run updates will appear here: https://bench.internal/runs/3749999999
Alex Kim: end of thread for now.
